passage: Abstract: "A frequent experimental flaw is the application of oversampling algorithms to the entire dataset, resulting in biased models and overly-optimistic estimates."
faulty: SMOTE (k = 5) is applied to all 1500 records; stratified 10-fold cross-validation with a 5-nearest-neighbour classifier then runs on the enlarged data; balanced accuracy (mean of sensitivity and specificity, pooled test-fold predictions including synthetic rows) is the statistic. Claim holds when balanced accuracy >= 0.65.
fixed: Stratified 10-fold cross-validation on the original 1500 records; SMOTE on the training folds only; balanced accuracy on the original test-fold records, pooled.
estimand: Faulty: balanced accuracy on test rows that include interpolations of training minority rows. Fixed: balanced accuracy on new original records.
model_family: 5-nearest-neighbour classifier on standardised variables, with SMOTE (k = 5). Chosen by me: the abstract names no classifier; k-NN is where synthetic-neighbour overlap bites hardest, and it is cheap.
sizes_note: Source sizes: not stated in the abstract (full text not open). 1500 x 20 = 30k values, the larger regime among my SAN18 briefs; check cost low (k-NN, 10 folds). Dependence on imbalance or n: not stated.
exploited_structure: A strongly unbalanced label distribution requiring many synthetic rows, which then sit next to their real parents across the folds.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the abstract gives no imbalance ratio; 9.0 (a 90/10 split) is proposed as typical

notes: Differs from B2B-03 in statistic (balanced accuracy vs F1), sample-size regime (1500 x 20 vs 600 x 12) and model. Guard minimum 2: one record of each class in the evaluated data.
